problem: Consider a matrix equation $A\,x={B}^{-1}\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\times 2$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
examples.problem: Consider a matrix equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d},$ where $A$ and $B$ are $10 \times 10$ non-singular matrices, while $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$ are $10 \times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $\mathbf{x}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse $B^{−1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\,\mathbf{d}$ by $B^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{10}\,x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+z+x=2 \\ -3z+y=3 \\ 2x+y=4-4z\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ y-3z=3 \\ 2x+y+4z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4+3)-(0+6)+(0-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & 1\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=11,y=-6,z=-3.$
